## 1. Program summary

S&P 500 Core Relative Allocation (SCRA) is a systematic, long-biased futures program built around a permanent U.S. large-cap equity core, with dynamic tilts into a diversified set of liquid futures markets whenever they are outperforming the core on a risk-adjusted basis. The objective is to compound at an equity-like return while holding realized risk within a controlled band through the cycle. The program is always net long equity; the tactical sleeve rotates around the core rather than replacing it.

## 2. Investment thesis / source of return

The program is built on three durable sources of return. The first is the equity risk premium — the long-run compensation for holding productive corporate assets, which has been the most reliably positive risk premium available to investors and anchors the portfolio permanently. The second is diversification across genuinely different risk premia: duration, real assets, and cross-market trend behave differently from equity across the economic cycle, and combining them improves the ratio of return to risk. The third is a relative-strength effect: leadership across markets persists longer than efficient-market intuition suggests, because capital reallocates slowly and investors under-react to shifts in which exposures are being rewarded. The program is designed to lean gently toward whatever is being rewarded on a risk-adjusted basis while never abandoning the equity core. These are structural and behavioral effects, not a forecast of any single market.

## 3. Universe & instruments

The program trades ten regulated, USD-denominated futures contracts spanning four economic roles: equity indices (S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000), real assets (gold, silver), the U.S. rates curve (2-, 5-, 10-year notes and the long bond), and digital assets (bitcoin). Each instrument represents a distinct macroeconomic exposure that belongs in a long-horizon allocation; short-term positioning vehicles and narrow sub-sector contracts are deliberately excluded.

Listed futures are used because they offer deep liquidity, transparent exchange pricing, capital efficiency, and regulatory suitability, with no single-name idiosyncratic risk. The S&P 500 is the permanent core and the benchmark against which every alternative's relative performance is judged.

## 4. Methodology (conceptual)

The approach has three elements, described here in mechanism only.

**Signal philosophy.** Each alternative market is continuously assessed on its recent risk-adjusted performance relative to the equity core. Markets that are persistently outperforming the core earn a larger allocation; markets that are not default back toward the core. The intent is to tilt toward durable, risk-adjusted leadership rather than to predict direction.

**Sizing philosophy.** Positions are scaled by their recent downside volatility so that each contributes a comparable amount of risk to the portfolio, and overall exposure is set by a dynamic-leverage mechanism that expands in calm, high-conviction conditions and contracts in stressed or weak-signal conditions. The goal of leverage is a consistent risk profile across regimes, not maximal return in any single moment.

**Cadence.** Signals are evaluated every trading day, but the portfolio is only traded when the implied change is material, under a no-trade discipline that limits turnover and transaction costs.

Specific lookback windows, thresholds, volatility targets, and sizing constants are proprietary and are not disclosed.

## 5. Risk management

Risk is managed at the position and portfolio level. Each position is sized to a comparable risk contribution through downside-volatility targeting, so no single market dominates the portfolio's outcome. The equity core always holds the residual weight, keeping the program net long equity at all times. Gross leverage is bounded, and the tactical sleeve is capped so the program cannot rotate away from its equity anchor.

Honest disclosure on drawdowns: because the allocation signal is backward-looking, the program reduces exposure only after sustained relative weakness, and it will take full equity drawdowns in fast bear markets. It is a risk-managed equity program, **not** a drawdown-defense product. In sharp risk-off episodes, exposure reduces with a lag rather than pre-emptively.

## 6. Portfolio construction & constraints

The portfolio is constructed as a permanent equity core plus a bounded tactical sleeve. The core holds the majority of risk at all times; only a capped fraction of the portfolio may rotate into the diversifying markets. Overall gross leverage is held within a defined range, and realized downside volatility is targeted within a moderate band rather than at a single fixed number. Positions are expressed in whole exchange-listed contracts. These are stated as policies and ranges; exact parameter values are not published.

## 7. Execution & operations

The program is executed systematically once per trading day by a fully automated engine. Orders are generated by fixed rules from the prior session's closing data and routed to Interactive Brokers; there is no discretionary intervention in the trade loop. Futures are traded on regulated exchanges operated by CME Group (CME, CBOT, COMEX). Positions are held at a regulated prime broker with independent daily mark-to-market pricing and segregated custody. Reconciliation, monitoring, and alerting run continuously, and the same engine that trades the account is the reference implementation of the strategy — there is no separate, more-favorable "model" track record.

## 8. Capacity & minimum investment

The program is offered through separately managed accounts. The suggested minimum for an effective deployment is approximately **US$500,000** — enough for positions to be expressed in whole contracts with acceptable granularity and for execution and financing costs to remain proportionate. Capacity is large: the markets traded are among the most liquid listed instruments in the world, so the strategy can scale materially before market impact becomes a consideration. New accounts are onboarded so that client positioning stays aligned with the manager's own live account.

## 9. Track record

The program runs live in a verified Interactive Brokers Financial Advisor sub-account, and the public track record begins at the migration to that structure — reported without adjustment, with no earlier development history stitched in. Live performance, current positioning, and a same-period benchmark comparison are published on the program's performance-attribution page: **[SCRA performance attribution](attribution.html)**. Because the live sample currently spans only a short period, statistics that require a longer window are shown as *accumulating* rather than annualized.

## 10. Key risks & disclaimers

::: {.callout-warning}
This program uses leverage and can experience meaningful drawdowns; it is designed for long-horizon investors who can tolerate equity-like volatility. It is not a drawdown-defense product and will participate in falling markets. Systematic models can underperform, and any model is a simplification that may behave unexpectedly in conditions unlike those that informed its design. Live and simulated results are not a guarantee of future performance; past performance — whether hypothetical or actual — does not predict future results. Nothing in this document is investment, legal, or tax advice, nor an offer to sell or a solicitation to buy any security or fund interest. All figures are in U.S. dollars unless stated otherwise.
:::
